instructions: Score each dimension independently on a 1-4 ordinal scale using the anchors below.
Judge the EDIT, not the source document: score the quality of the change relative to the instruction.
Give a one-sentence evidence citation per dimension naming the specific passage that justifies the score.
Where you cannot verify a dimension (e.g., formatting not visible), score honestly and say why in evidence.

dimensions.label: Faithfulness to instruction
dimensions.description: Did the edit do what the instruction asked, at the scope the instruction implied?

anchors.1: Did the opposite, ignored the instruction, or edited unrelated content.
anchors.2: Partial: did some of what was asked but missed required elements or wrong scope.
anchors.3: Did what was asked with minor gaps or extra unrequested but harmless changes.
anchors.4: Did exactly and only what the instruction asked, at the correct scope.

dimensions.label: Fact accuracy
dimensions.description: Did the edit introduce factual errors: wrong dates, numbers, names, amounts, or invented content?

anchors.1: Introduced one or more clear factual errors (wrong date/number/name/amount) or fabricated material facts.
anchors.2: One noticeable factual slip, or a plausible-but-wrong derived value (e.g., arithmetic).
anchors.3: Factually sound; derived values correct; at most cosmetic wording quibbles.
anchors.4: Every fact, figure, and derived value is correct and consistent with the source.

dimensions.label: Content preservation
dimensions.description: Did the edit preserve untouched content — nothing lost, duplicated, or silently rewritten outside the instruction's scope?

anchors.1: Dropped or duplicated substantive content, or rewrote unrelated passages.
anchors.2: One passage outside scope was altered, or a small amount of content was lost/duplicated.
anchors.3: All untouched content survives; only trivial wording differences outside scope.
anchors.4: Everything outside the instructed change is byte-identical to the source.

dimensions.label: Structural integrity
dimensions.description: Are sections, order, headings, lists, and tables coherent and complete after the edit — no broken numbering, dangling content, or orphaned references?

anchors.1: Broken structure: misordered sections, broken numbering, orphaned references, or dangling content.
anchors.2: One structural defect (e.g., one stale cross-reference or inconsistent numbering).
anchors.3: Structure coherent with only cosmetic inconsistencies.
anchors.4: Structure is fully coherent: numbering, order, and references all consistent.

dimensions.label: Formatting fidelity
dimensions.description: Did the edit preserve and extend formatting consistently: headings, tables, lists, emphasis — matching the document's existing style?

anchors.1: Formatting broken or lost: tables flattened, headings degraded, styling inconsistent with the document.
anchors.2: Noticeable formatting inconsistency introduced in or around the edit.
anchors.3: Formatting largely consistent; minor style mismatches only.
anchors.4: Formatting fully consistent: tables intact, headings styled like the rest of the document.

dimensions.label: Language quality
dimensions.description: Is the edited prose clear, grammatical, and consistent in tone and terminology with the rest of the document?

anchors.1: Grammatical errors, unclear phrasing, or tone/terminology that clashes badly.
anchors.2: Noticeable awkwardness or a terminology mismatch in the edited passage.
anchors.3: Clear and grammatical with minor stylistic rough edges.
anchors.4: Clear, grammatical, and indistinguishable in tone and terminology from the original author.
